SNIPPER 1.0.1

Double-click Snipper.exe. No installation required.

Click New snip, drag an area, and release. Pen is selected automatically.
Ctrl+C copies the image with all annotations. Capturing never automatically copies.
Ctrl+S saves a PNG; Ctrl+Shift+S chooses a new filename.

Pen: draw with different widths and colors.
Circle/Arrow: drag to create; choose a color.
Use the small arrow beside Circle, Arrow, Check, and Line to choose a style.
Arrows: classic, outlined with a black border, curved gloss, or straight gloss.
Line: solid, dashed, or dotted. Hold Shift to snap its angle; L selects Line.
Check: click to place a green boxed check or drag to size it.
Select: move stickers; drag corners to resize, or arrow/line endpoints to turn.
Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y: undo / redo. Delete removes the selected annotation.
Draw and Shapes have separate toolbar groups, with shapes aligned to the right.
Undo/redo sits beside New snip. Hover for hints and shortcuts.
Color, stroke width, and zoom sit in their own row. Copy confirms with "Copied!".
Each tool remembers its own last color and style, including after File > Exit.
Preferences save on close/exit only. New captures still start with Pen.

Settings > Keyboard shortcut changes the global snipping shortcut.
Default: Ctrl+Alt+S. Keep the app running for the global shortcut.
Hover a menu and press the shortcut: the screen freezes before selection or save prompts.

Closing the window leaves a small tray process and releases the screenshot.
Click the tray icon to snip. File > Exit quits entirely.
Settings > Run at sign-in is optional and disabled by default.

Keep the app in a writable folder; JackSnip.ini is created beside it when
you save shortcut settings. Keep the accompanying runtime notices if sharing.
